name: Ramidreju (Mediterranean Monsters (Pathfinder RPG))
body:
Ramidreju
CR 1/2

This green, weasel-like creature has a long, snake-like body, a small boar-like head with long tusks, and yellow eyes.

XP 200
N Small magical beast
Init +6; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, treasure sense; Perception +1

DEFENSE

AC 13, touch 13, flat-footed 11 (+2 Dex, +1 size)
hp 7 (1d10+2)
Fort +4, Ref +4, Will +1

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., burrow 10 ft.
Melee gore +1 (1d8–1)

STATISTICS

Str 9, Dex 15, Con 14, Int 5, Wis 12, Cha 6
Base Atk +1; CMB –1; CMD 11 (15 vs. trip)
Feats Improved Initiative
Skills Stealth +10
SQ healing fur, magic bile

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Healing Fur (Su)

Once per day as an immediate action, a ramidreju can heal 1d8 hit points to a creature that touches its fur.

Magic Bile (Su)

Once per day as a standard action, the ramidreju can produce bile another creature can drink. For 4 rounds after drinking the bile, a creature gains a +1 enhancement bonus to Armor Class. However, the bile is poisonous.

Ramidreju Bile: Ingested; save Fort DC 12; frequency 1/round for 4 rounds; effect sickened for 1 round; cure 1 save. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Treasure Sense (Su)

A ramidreju can sense gold, gems, and other valuables within 30 feet as if using the scent ability.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate mountains and plains
Organization solitary, pair, or nest (2-4)
Treasure standard

A ramidreju’s green fur sometimes has black stripes, and while its bright coloring might suggests a poisonous nature, it in fact possess marvelous healing properties in its fur and bile.

Ramidrejus are typically found in the mountains and grasslands and grow to be 3 feet long but rarely exceed 40 pounds.

Ramidreju are known for digging deep, extensive burrows with their tusks, often unearthing gold and other treasure with an uncanny sense for finding lost things. They are elusive and difficult to capture but sometimes can be befriended, but dealing with them can be dangerous. Notable stories ramidrejus who helps young children find hidden treasure in exchange for their help escaping from a trap. Ramidrejus are sometimes tamed by goblins, who value them for their ability to seek out treasure. However, legends also warn of greedy folk who have captured ramidrejus for this purpose and not treated them well, bringing a curse upon themselves and leading to their downfall.
